instructions:
# httprouter

High-performance radix-tree routing for Go.

## What this skill does

- Registers typed routes with :param path segments.
- Dispatches by HTTP method automatically.
- Wraps handlers with middleware the standard library way.
- Serves 404/405 with method-specific handling.

## When to use

- A Go service needs fast routing without framework weight.
- You want explicit path parameters instead of string parsing.
- Serving REST endpoints with clean method separation.

## Real commands

```bash
# Install
go get github.com/julienschmidt/httprouter@latest

# Build, vet, test
go build -o app .
go vet ./...
go test ./...

# Run and hit a param route
go run . &
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/users/42
```

## Router setup

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "github.com/julienschmidt/httprouter"
)

func Hello(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, ps httprouter.Params) {
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello, %s!", ps.ByName("name"))
}

func main() {
    router := httprouter.New()
    router.GET("/hello/:name", Hello)
    router.POST("/users", CreateUser)
    router.PUT("/users/:id", UpdateUser)
    router.DELETE("/users/:id", DeleteUser)
    http.ListenAndServe(":8080", router)
}
```

## Middleware wrapper

```go
func logging(next httprouter.Handle) httprouter.Handle {
    return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, ps httprouter.Params) {
        log.Printf("%s %s", r.Method, r.URL.Path)
        next(w, r, ps)
    }
}

router.GET("/users/:id", logging(GetUser))
```

## Testing

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/hello/world
go test -bench=. -benchmem ./...
```

## Best practices

- Path params are matched in a single segment; use `:name` not `*` for required parts.
- Wrap handlers with standard `func(http.Handler, ...) http.Handler` style for reuse.
- Set `router.RedirectTrailingSlash = true` consciously; it can surprise clients.
- Keep handlers httprouter.Handle-typed to use Params without globals.

## Example exchange

```
User: Add a GET /users/:id route.
Agent: router.GET("/users/:id", func(w, r, ps) { id := ps.ByName("id") ... })
```
